title: Operator-mediated 'Nudge' Enactor for Safe Recommendation Adoption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an operator-mediated enactor that applies batching/caching recommendations as low-risk 'nudges' rather than hard commits. The enactor will: 1) stage a soft-apply that shadows traffic and collects end-to-end telemetry, 2) run a short micro-rollout (traffic slices under operator control) with automatic SLO and quality checks, 3) surface an approval UI and optional escrow hold for operator acknowledgement before wide commit, and 4) provide automated rollback playbooks when thresholds are breached. Key goals: reduce manual toil for low-risk cost recs, maintain strict latency/quality SLOs, and provide transparent audit and operator control. This ticket focuses on the orchestration layer, operator UI hooks, and integration points with telemetry guardrails and the config store.
acceptance_criteria: A staging mode where recommendation changes are applied to a shadowed runtime path and generate a full request/response telemetry stream
A micro-rollout controller that can split 1%-10% of traffic to the recommended config and evaluate pre-configured metrics for at least N=2000 tokens per variant
Operator UI shows a clear diff, expected cost delta, risk score, and a one-click 'Escrow & Approve' button; approvals are recorded in audit logs
Automatic rollback executes within 60s of breach detection and marks the event in the rollout timeline with root-cause hints
Integrations with Optimize's suggestion engine so suggested configs can be 'nudged' automatically into staging with operator-notification
End-to-end tests that simulate high-latency downstream model variants and assert rollback and alerting behavior
tasks: Design operator 'nudge' UX and approval flow with PM/Design (mockups linked)
Implement shadowing proxy and telemetry tagging for staged configs
Implement micro-rollout traffic splitter and throttling DSL
Add policy evaluator that runs SLO checks (latency, 99th token RT, cost delta, quality regression heuristics)
Wire approval/escrow state into config store and audit log
Create automated rollback playbook and playbook runbook doc
Add unit/integration tests and a simulated traffic harness for canary scenarios
Prepare runbook for oncall and ops handoff

2026-02-02: Design review — Design suggested a two-row diff (behavioral + cost) and an 'Escrow' state instead of immediate commit. Connor to prototype the UX. (Design feedback)

2026-03-04: Simulation harness run — small config that increases batching saved ~22% cost but increased P95 latency by 6ms; rollout policy thresholds caught regression and triggered automatic revert. Test passed. (QA)
2026-03-08: Design/PM requested clearer operator guidance for 'acceptable risk' — added a risk scoring card to the UI. Implementing. (Connor)
2026-03-10: RFC draft linked; seeking review from runtime and infra teams. Next: PR for micro-rollout controller. (Aisha)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive batching reduces unit cost but can increase tail latency; we favor conservative thresholds for production vs a more permissive staging environment.
Decided on 'soft shadow then micro-rollout then escrow' flow instead of blind auto-commit to minimize blast radius and preserve operator trust.
We will prefer shorter micro-rollouts (1–3 hours) with automatic rollback instead of long quiet launches to accelerate learning while limiting exposure.
risks_mitigation: Risk: False-positive regressions from noisy telemetry — Mitigation: require multi-metric agreement across latency and quality signals before auto-revert
Risk: Approval bottleneck causing delayed cost savings — Mitigation: create a 'low-risk' policy tier that allows staging and auto-suggest but requires operator acknowledgement for production commit
Risk: Escrow token compromise — Mitigation: KMS-backed short-lived tokens and audit trail
test_plan: Unit tests for traffic splitter and policy evaluator
Integration tests with shadow proxy and telemetry ingestion pipeline
Chaos tests that inject increased model latency and assert rollback behavior
E2E simulation that measures cost delta and validates risk scoring card
open_questions: How many tokens per variant should be the minimum for statistically meaningful quality checks? (current default: 2000)
Should we expose an 'auto-approve' predicate for well-vetted recommenders after operator certification? (PM asked to evaluate)
What rate-limits should apply to rapid successive rollouts for the same customer to avoid oscillation?
